title: Room-temperature polariton supersolids
authors: Yuanhao Gong, Jingwen Ma, Shuang Zhang, Xiaobo Yin, Xiang Zhang
abstract: Exploring exotic quantum phases of matter at room temperature represents a frontier challenge in modern physics. The supersolid phase, uniquely merging crystalline order with frictionless superfluid flow, stands among the most intriguing macroscopic quantum phenomena. However, all previous demonstrations of supersolidity, whether in ultracold atomic gases or III-V semiconductor-based polariton systems, have been strictly confined to cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the observation of room-temperature supersolids in photonic-crystal polariton condensates. By integrating a room-temperature-stable perovskite semiconductor with a dispersion-engineered photonic-crystal waveguide, we create a polariton condensate with multi-mode dispersion landscapes and pronounced parametric nonlinearities. Above a critical condensation density, the interacting condensates spontaneously break continuous translational symmetry, creating a non-rigid supersolid phase that simultaneously exhibits emergent crystalline order and global quantum coherence. This work establishes a room-temperature platform for investigating quantum hydrodynamics and developing coherent quantum simulation devices.
summary: This paper reports the groundbreaking observation of a supersolid phase in polariton condensates operating at room temperature. By engineering a hybrid perovskite/photonic-crystal device, the authors created a platform where the condensate spontaneously develops both crystalline order and superfluid coherence. This achievement opens a new, accessible avenue for studying fundamental quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish and characterize a room-temperature platform for observing the supersolid phase, which combines crystalline order with superfluid flow.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a room-temperature polariton supersolid in a hybrid perovskite/photonic-crystal device, evidenced by simultaneous crystalline order and quantum coherence.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling of nonlinear dynamics with advanced experimental techniques like angle-resolved optical microscopy and momentum-space quantum coincidence measurements.
model_or_system: The system uses a polariton condensate formed in a photonic-crystal waveguide integrated with a room-temperature perovskite semiconductor. The physics is modeled by an effective Hamiltonian describing parametric squeezing between counter-propagating modes.
key_observables: Simultaneous observation of crystalline order (DLRO) and quantum coherence (ODLRO); distinct spectral peaks at finite momenta ($\pm k_{	ext{ss}}$); nonlinear density scaling laws ($n_1 \propto n_0^{0.97}$).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation; critical condensation density ($P_{	ext{th}}^{	ext{SS}}$); the ratio of parametric gain to dissipation rate.
main_assumptions: The condensate ($\psi_0$) is treated as a classical coherent field; the perovskite film's exciton properties are assumed stable at ambient conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, the spectral evolution across two distinct pump thresholds (BEC and SS), and quantitative plots showing the density scaling relationship between the supersolid and condensate components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the challenge of room-temperature supersolidity to detailing the hybrid device construction, presenting theoretical models for the nonlinear dynamics, and finally reporting experimental measurements confirming the supersolid signatures.
why_interesting: This work bridges the gap between cryogenic quantum phenomena and ambient conditions using solid-state photonics, offering a highly accessible platform for studying complex quantum hydrodynamics and phase transitions relevant to AMO physics.
